title: Simultaneous Sentek and ML3 Calibration
author: Sarah SG Garre
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jm5ck86

steps.title: Collect Soil Samples from Profile Pit
steps.instruction: Dig a soil profile pit to access target horizons (e.g., 25, 55, and 85 cm deep).

substeps.instruction: Sample at least three Kopecky rings per horizon to determine bulk density.
Collect 31,416 cm³ of soil per container needed for calibration for each horizon and replicate (calculated as pi*(40/2)² * 25).
Collect an additional 20% of soil as extra.
Label boxes by horizon, keep them separated, and close for transport.

steps.title: Determine Soil Bulk Density
steps.instruction: Measure the bulk density of the soil for each horizon using a ring of known volume (250 cm³).

substeps.instruction: Take a soil sample with the ring and cut excess soil from the top and bottom.
Weigh the sample and dry in an oven at 105°C for approximately 48 hours.
Cool the sample in a desiccator.
Weigh the dry sample and calculate bulk density as: mass of dry sample / known volume.

steps.title: Prepare Soil for Column Packing
steps.instruction: Calculate and prepare the required mass of soil for a waterproof cylinder (diameter 0.35m, height 0.25m).

substeps.instruction: Calculate required soil weight: W soil = V column x BD soil.
Oven-dry the calculated W soil plus a 10% margin at 45°C for 3 days (separate soil into different boxes to accelerate drying).
Pound and screen the required mass through a 5 mm sieve.

steps.title: Assemble and Pack Soil Column
steps.instruction: Pack the soil into the waterproof cylinder to a specific target density.

substeps.instruction: Insert the cap to waterproof the Access Tube and Sentek Sensor.
Weigh the unfilled column container, the Sentek Sensor, and the Access Tube.
Mark the Access Tube every 2 cm.
Place the Sentek Access Tube in the center of the column and stabilize it.
Calculate the mass of soil required for a 2 cm depth using the formula from step 3.
Spread soil uniformly and pack down to a thickness of 2 cm (use a ring to pack soil near the Access Tube).
Repeat packing in 2 cm increments until the container is full.
Measure and record the final filled column weight.

steps.title: Configure Data Acquisition System
steps.instruction: Set up the computer and logger for data collection.

substeps.instruction: Install 'Probe Configuration Utility' and 'LoggerNet 4.4.2' on the computer.
Connect CR6 to an external 12V power source and connect the computer to the CR6 via RJ45 using a router via LoggerNet.
Connect balances and ML3 probe to the CR6Series.
Program data collection intervals: every 15 minutes for the balance and every 20 seconds for the probe.

steps.title: Perform Water Normalization
steps.instruction: Normalize the Sentek sensors using a water bath.

substeps.instruction: Identify each probe with a tag.
Insert the Sentek Sensor into the Access Tube and connect them.
Connect the programming cable to the TTL port and supply 12V power.
Fill the column with water to check for leaks.
Insert the probe into the water normalization container.
Use the Probe Configuration Utility to auto-detect sensors and set depths.
Click the Low/Water column header to normalize all sensors (or do so individually if the container only supports one sensor at a time), ensuring the sphere-of-influence is fully surrounded by water.
Transcribe results.

steps.title: Perform Air Normalization
steps.instruction: Normalize the Sentek sensors using an empty container.

substeps.instruction: Insert the Sentek Sensor into the Access Tube and connect them.
Connect the programming cable to the TTL port and supply 12V power.
Use the Probe Configuration Utility to auto-detect sensors and set depths.
Position the tube in an empty container, staying clear of cables.
Click the High/Air column header to normalize all sensors one by one.
Transcribe results.

steps.title: Calibrate ML3 and Sentek Probes
steps.instruction: Measure probe responses at specific soil moisture levels.

substeps.instruction: Insert the ML3 probe into the column.
Read and record the ML3 probe voltage and the column weight.
Insert the EnviroSCAN probe to 7.5 cm depth (middle of column) in the Access Tube and connect.
Enter variable data (NumberBox, provenance, moisture content, original depth) in the software.
Launch the program for normalization; record at least 3 readings (preferably 10 by setting collection time to 1 minute and leaving the probe for 10 minutes).
Synchronize logger, computer, and stopwatch times (e.g., balance weight every 15 min, probe voltage every 20 sec).
Record the column weight for each sensor and repeat for all sensors needing calibration.

steps.title: Repeat for Multiple Moisture Levels
steps.instruction: Calibrate the sensors across a range of soil moisture contents (e.g., 5%, 15%, 25%, and 40%).

substeps.instruction: Remove soil from the column.
Spread soil on a plastic sheet and mix with a measured volume of water thoroughly.
Repeat the assembly and measurement steps (Steps 4, 8, 9, 10) for each moisture level.

steps.title: Determine Volumetric Water Content
steps.instruction: Use Kopecky rings to verify the actual volumetric water content and bulk density.

substeps.instruction: Remove soil down to the required depth level.

Drive the Kopecky ring as close as possible to the access tube without touching it, aligning the center of the ring with the center of the sensor's sphere of influence (top of ring level with soil platform).
Use a sampling ring tube extension to avoid soil compaction.
Obtain wet and dry oven weights to determine volumetric water content and bulk density.

steps.title: Derive Calibration Equations
steps.instruction: Process the collected data to create calibration curves for both probe types.

substeps.instruction: For Sentek: Convert raw counts (FS) to Scaled Frequency (SF) using SF = (FA - FS) / (FA - FW), where FA is Air Count and FW is Water Count.
Plot SF (Y-axis) against volumetric water content (X-axis) in replicate pairs per depth level.
Fit a calibration curve (SF = AqB + C) and perform regression analysis to find A, B, and C coefficients.
For ML3: Use the linear equation √ε = a0 + a1 x WC to generate coefficients a0 and a1 (refer to ML3 calibration manual).
